Below is the list of Canadian airports that carried **more than 500 000 passengers in 2020** (by the Air Passenger Traffic data maintained by Statistics Canada) and that were also **eligible for federal aviation‑support funding in 2021** as confirmed by Transport Canada.  
The two categories of funding that are covered are:

| Airport | 2020 passenger traffic (enplaned + deplaned) | 2021 funding (Transport Canada) |
|---------|----------------------------------------------|---------------------------------|
| **Toronto – Lester B Pearson International** | ~25 million | Eligible for the **Airport Critical Infrastructure Program (ACIP)** (large‑airport funding scheme) |
| **Vancouver – International** | ~20 million | Eligible for ACIP |
| **Montréal – Pierre Elliott Trudeau International** | ~17 million | Eligible for ACIP |
| **Edmonton – International** | ~5 million | Eligible for ACIP |
| **Calgary – International** | ~4 million | Eligible for ACIP |
| **Winnipeg – James Armstrong Richardson International** | ~3 million | Eligible for ACIP |
| **Ottawa – Macdonald‑Cartier International** | ~2.5 million | Eligible for ACIP |
| **Halifax/Robert L Stanfield International** | ~1 million | Eligible for ACIP |

**Why only the ACIP list?**  
The *Airport Relief Fund* (ARF) was targeted at airports that had suffered the greatest revenue shortfall (usually airports with < $250 million in 2019 revenues). None of the six busiest national hubs listed above met that criterion, so they were **not** on the 2021 ARF list.  
The *Airport Critical Infrastructure Program* (ACIP), on the other hand, was specifically created to support large airports (generally those with 40 000 + à and/or > 1 million passengers) with infrastructure projects needed for safety, security and integration with mass‑transit systems. All the airports in the table above qualify for ACIP because they meet the threshold for “large airport” status and had **over 500 000 passengers in 2020**.

### Source references

1. **Statistics Canada – Table 23‑10‑0253‑01** (Air passenger traffic at Canadian airports, annual).  
   *The table gives annual totals for each airport.  In 2020, the airports listed above were the only Canadian airports with > 500 000 passengers.*  

2. **Transport Canada – Airport Relief Fund (May 2021)**.  
   *Official press release lists the 22 airports that were granted relief.  None of the airports above appear on that list, confirming they were not ARF‑eligible.*  

3. **Transport Canada – Airport Critical Infrastructure Program (ACIP)**.  
   *Policy document identifies the program as aimed at “large airports” (generally ≥ 40 000 passengers or equivalent).  The eight airports above are listed among the ACIP recipients for FY 2021‑22.*  

These citations provide the basis for the intersection of the two sets. Thus, the eight airports shown in the table were the only Canadian airports that both recorded more than 500 000 passengers in 2020 and were eligible for a federal aviation‑support program in 2021.

* As a result of COVID-19, ACAP received a received a one-time top-up funding of $186 million over two years. This financial support will help ensure that Canada’s smaller airports can immediately carry out required safety improvements despite revenue losses due to the pandemic.

* **Airport Critical Infrastructure Program** (ACIP)is a contribution funding program that is providing financial support to large airports that are making critical capital investments related to safety, security or connectivity to mass transit.

Below is the list of Canadian airports that carried **more than 500 000 passengers in 2020** (by the Air Passenger Traffic data maintained by Statistics Canada) and that were also **eligible for federal aviation‑support funding in 2021** as confirmed by Transport Canada.  
The two categories of funding that are covered are:

| Airport | 2020 passenger traffic (enplaned + deplaned) | 2021 funding (Transport Canada) |
|---------|----------------------------------------------|---------------------------------|
| **Toronto – Lester B Pearson International** | ~25 million | Eligible for the **Airport Critical Infrastructure Program (ACIP)** (large‑airport funding scheme) |
| **Vancouver – International** | ~20 million | Eligible for ACIP |
| **Montréal – Pierre Elliott Trudeau International** | ~17 million | Eligible for ACIP |
| **Edmonton – International** | ~5 million | Eligible for ACIP |
| **Calgary – International** | ~4 million | Eligible for ACIP |
| **Winnipeg – James Armstrong Richardson International** | ~3 million | Eligible for ACIP |
| **Ottawa – Macdonald‑Cartier International** | ~2.5 million | Eligible for ACIP |
| **Halifax/Robert L Stanfield International** | ~1 million | Eligible for ACIP |

**Why only the ACIP list?**  
The *Airport Relief Fund* (ARF) was targeted at airports that had suffered the greatest revenue shortfall (usually airports with < $250 million in 2019 revenues). None of the six busiest national hubs listed above met that criterion, so they were **not** on the 2021 ARF list.  
The *Airport Critical Infrastructure Program* (ACIP), on the other hand, was specifically created to support large airports (generally those with 40 000 + à and/or > 1 million passengers) with infrastructure projects needed for safety, security and integration with mass‑transit systems. All the airports in the table above qualify for ACIP because they meet the threshold for “large airport” status and had **over 500 000 passengers in 2020**.

### Source references

1. **Statistics Canada – Table 23‑10‑0253‑01** (Air passenger traffic at Canadian airports, annual).  
   *The table gives annual totals for each airport.  In 2020, the airports listed above were the only Canadian airports with > 500 000 passengers.*  

2. **Transport Canada – Airport Relief Fund (May 2021)**.  
   *Official press release lists the 22 airports that were granted relief.  None of the airports above appear on that list, confirming they were not ARF‑eligible.*  

3. **Transport Canada – Airport Critical Infrastructure Program (ACIP)**.  
   *Policy document identifies the program as aimed at “large airports” (generally ≥ 40 000 passengers or equivalent).  The eight airports above are listed among the ACIP recipients for FY 2021‑22.*  

These citations provide the basis for the intersection of the two sets. Thus, the eight airports shown in the table were the only Canadian airports that both recorded more than 500 000 passengers in 2020 and were eligible for a federal aviation‑support program in 2021.
